intended_object: The multiplicative submonoid of ℕ consisting of positive integers all of whose prime divisors lie in a given set S of primes (S-supported integers), equivalently the submonoid generated by S. Inferred from docstring and module doc.
explanation: The body is `Submonoid.closure` of the image of S in ℕ. By unique factorization this is exactly {n > 0 | every prime p ∣ n lies in S}, as the library proves in `mem_primeSupportedIndices_iff`. The edge cases are right: 1 is included as the empty product, 0 is excluded, and S = ∅ gives {1}. S may be any set of primes, not just a finite one, which is the right generality for supernatural and profinite indices. Mathlib's `Nat.factoredNumbers` is the same set but takes only a Finset and is a plain Set rather than a submonoid, so it is narrower, not broader. The definition is therefore faithful.
